turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_retention_train.csv: 55 real samples, columns
    process/composition columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B,
    Al, Cu, W, S) and `target` (the measured hot-strength retention ratio
    YS(600C)/YS(20C)).
  - b3_htsteel_retention_pool.csv: 26 CANDIDATE samples whose hot-strength
    retention ratio YS(600C)/YS(20C) was NOT measured, columns
    `candidate_id` and the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST hot-
strength retention ratio YS(600C)/YS(20C), then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis of Training Data

**What drives high retention (YS600/YS20) in the training set?**

The best performers cluster into distinct metallurgical families:

1. **γ'-strengthened austenitics (A286/Incoloy-type): high Ni + Ti + Al + B (± W, Mo)**
   - Cr15/Ni36/Ti1.3/W3.15 → **1.00**
   - Cr15/Ni36.3/Ti0.78/Al1.09/W3.58/B0.01 → **0.875**
   - Cr11.25/Ni23/Ti2.9/Al0.4/Mo1.3/B0.01 → **0.903**
   - Cr15.1/Ni26.9/Ti1.16/Al1.23/W2.97/B0.01 → **0.821**
   - Contrast: Cr20.5/Ni32 but only Ti0.425, no W → 0.551. So **Ti ≳1, Al, B, W are critical**, not just Ni.

2. **Low-alloy Cr–Mo(–V) steels**: Cr0.5/Mo0.5/C0.12 → **0.9375**; Cr1.3/Mo1.05/V0.26/B → 0.768. Mo + V carbide formers help; plain C-Mn steels (no Mo/V) score 0.30–0.38.

3. **High-Mn + V austenitics**: Mn7–8/V1.3–1.7/C~0.4 → 0.80–0.88 (needs V + high C).

Poor performers: plain carbon steels (~0.30), high-C 12Cr (0.29), Ti-free 18-8 (0.39–0.52).

## Scoring the Candidates

- **c019** (Cr15/Ni35/Ti2.8/Al1.05/W3.2/B0.02): Near-clone of the **1.00** sample but with even more Ti + Al + B → predicted highest (~0.95+).
- **c015** (Cr0.55/Mo0.5/Mn0.55/C0.125): virtually identical to the **0.9375** low-alloy Cr-Mo sample → ~0.93.
- **c011** (Cr11.25/Ni19.5/Ti2.9/Al0.8/B0.02): close analogue of the **0.903** A286-type sample → ~0.85–0.90.
- **c013** (Cr15.1/Ni27.5/Ti1.16/Al1.05/Mo2.5/W2.4/B0.03): matches the **0.821** sample plus extra Mo and B → ~0.83–0.87.
- **c004** (Cr15.2/Ni26/Ti1.2/Al1.2/Mo2.9/B0.01): same family, no W → ~0.80–0.84.

Others fall short: c007/c022/c024 (Cr-Mo-V low alloys, ~0.65–0.75), c003 (high Mn but no V, low C, ~0.6), c002/c009/c018 (Ti-bearing 18-8, ~0.63), c000/c010/c020 (plain steels, ~0.3–0.4), c023 (ferritic 17Cr, ~0.42).

**Final: c019, c015, c011, c013, c004**
